title: The KILLDOZER Rampage
summary: Josh and Chuck cover the 2004 Killdozer rampage in Granby, Colorado, in which muffler shop owner Marv Hemeyer, after years of feuds with the town, the Docheff concrete plant family, and the Thompson family, armored a Komatsu bulldozer with steel and concrete and drove it through downtown, destroying buildings including the town hall, a bank, a newspaper office, and the Thompson properties before being stopped by a gunshot inside the machine. They cover the background disputes (a gambling referendum, a land sale, a sewer line requirement), his preparations, the rampage itself, the aftermath and rebuilding, and the name "killdozer." Ticket plugs for upcoming tour dates and a listener mail about whistling in theaters close out the episode.

segments.title: Tour dates and ticket plugs
segments.summary: Chuck and Josh promote upcoming live shows in Chicago, Minneapolis, and Indianapolis and where to buy tickets.

segments.title: Introduction to the Killdozer episode
segments.summary: The hosts introduce the Killdozer topic, the documentary Tread, and set the scene in Granby, Colorado, in 2004.

segments.title: Setting and introduction of Marv Hemeyer
segments.summary: Chuck describes the June 4, 2004 rampage and introduces Marv Hemeyer, a muffler shop owner and former Air Force member who had feuds with townspeople.

segments.title: Gambling referendum and newspaper feud
segments.summary: Hemeyer moved to Grand Lake, where he lost a vote on legalized gambling and fought with the local newspaper.

segments.title: Land purchase and Docheff dispute
segments.summary: Hemeyer bought land at foreclosure in 1992 and clashed with the Docheff family over a planned sale and appraisals.

segments.title: Muffler shop trade-off and access dispute
segments.summary: The Docheffs offered a trade for a highway lot, Hemeyer objected, the concrete plant expansion was opposed, and the hosts correct the myth that his access was cut off.

segments.title: Sewer line dispute and fines
segments.summary: Hemeyer's property lacked a sewer connection, leading to dumping into a concrete mixer and ditch, a town fine, and his refusal to pay for a sewer tie-in.

segments.title: Thompson family feud and shop closure
segments.summary: The Thompson family feud is introduced, and Hemeyer closes his shop in 2002, selling the property but keeping a shed for his bulldozer.

segments.title: Break
segments.summary: Brief break before the next segment.

segments.title: Modifying the Komatsu bulldozer
segments.summary: Hemeyer bought a Komatsu bulldozer at auction in California and spent about a year modifying it in a shed on the property sold to a trash company.

segments.title: Hemeyer's personal life and motives
segments.summary: Hemeyer's fiance Tricia McDonald and the breakup, his father's death, and his savvy transfer of the sale money to relatives are discussed.

segments.title: Armor, gun ports, and cameras
segments.summary: The hosts describe the steel and concrete superstructure, gun ports, rifles, and cameras, and argue against the claim that he only wanted property destruction.

segments.title: Hit list, tapes, and the 'reasonable men' quote
segments.summary: A hit list of targeted buildings is described, along with Hemeyer's cassette tapes to his brother and his anti-Catholic and reasonable-man statements.

segments.title: The rampage begins at the concrete plant
segments.summary: The rampage begins at the Docheff concrete plant, where Cody Docheff tries to stop the machine, a deputy rides atop it, and the machine crashes through highway barriers.

segments.title: Town hall, bank, and newspaper destroyed
segments.summary: The machine destroys the town hall, a bank branch, and the newspaper office, with people narrowly escaping.

segments.title: Thompson property destruction and propane company threat
segments.summary: Thelma Thompson's house and the Thompson business are destroyed, and Hemeyer fires at a propane company's tanks and an electrical transformer, a threat the hosts discuss.

segments.title: Machine stopped at hardware store and aftermath
segments.summary: The machine's treads slip into a basement at Gamble's hardware store, a gunshot is heard inside, and the next day a charge fails to breach the armor.

segments.title: Damage, dismantling, and rebuilding
segments.summary: The hosts describe the damage, the lack of casualties, the dismantling of the machine, and the town's rebuilding and community response.

segments.title: Folk hero debate and Killdozer Day
segments.summary: The hosts discuss the folk hero narrative among some right-leaning circles and their own changed views after reading the Dozer Manifesto webcomic.

segments.title: Origin of the name Killdozer
segments.summary: The hosts discuss the origin of the name killdozer, including the Madison band and the 1974 TV movie based on a Theodore Sturgeon story.

segments.title: Listener mail: theater whistling superstition
segments.summary: A listener shares the theater superstition about whistling, tied to stagehands who were former sailors using whistle signals.

segments.title: Sign-off
segments.summary: Josh asks for listener mail and the hosts sign off with the iHeartRadio credit.
